items.title: Sultan Nazrin calls for less political rivalry among Malaysia’s Muslim leaders
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 25 — The unity of Muslims is facing growing challenges due to differences in politics, religious schools of thought, race and personal interests, Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Shah said. “These include Islamic economics, Islamic finance, the halal industry, waqf, digital dakwah and strengthening family institutions. Also present were the Raja Permaisuri of Perak Tuanku Zara Salim, Perak Raja Muda Raja Jaafar Raja Muda Musa and Raja Di Hilir Raja Iskandar Dzurkarnain Sultan Idris Shah.

items.title: Syed Azman humbled, Ruzita champions PwD inclusion after receiving Maulidur Rasul awards
items.summary: SERDANG: Weststar Group founder and managing director Tan Sri Dr Syed Azman Syed Ibrahim said he initially felt unqualified to receive the national-level Maulidur Rasul Tokoh Perdana award as he was not a religious scholar. Syed Azman said he was surprised when informed of his selection and initially questioned whether he was suitable for the honour. "Rasulullah often showed compassion towards people with disabilities, but in today's society we see the PwD community often being marginalised.

items.title: Oil steadies as investors weigh impact of latest US sanctions on Iran
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Oil prices recovered ground on Tuesday after settling down more than two per cent in the previous session, with investors assessing the impact of the latest US sanctions against Iran. Brent crude futures rose 27 cents, or 0.3 per cent, to US$92.44 a barrel by 0330 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude was up 37 cents, or 0.4 per cent, at US$85.38. Both contracts settled lower on Monday, with US crude oil falling to a one-week low on profit taking after prices rallied over the previous two weeks.

items.title: Rahim Razali honoured with Perak Tokoh Pengamal Media award
items.summary: IPOH: Film director and actor Datuk Abdul Rahim Mohd Razali received the Tokoh Pengamal Media award at the state-level Maulidur Rasul celebrations here today. Sultan Nazrin, who arrived at 11am, was accompanied by Raja Permaisuri Perak Tuanku Zara Salim. Also present were Raja Muda Perak Raja Jaafar Raja Muda Musa, Raja DiHilir Perak Raja Iskandar Dzulkarnain Idris Shah and Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad.

items.title: Ayob Khan: Tokoh Wira Negara Award honours sacrifices of police personnel
items.summary: SERDANG: For Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay, the national-level Maulidur Rasul Tokoh Wira Negara Award recognises not only his service but also the sacrifices of police personnel in protecting the country. "Indeed, I did not expect to be chosen to receive the National-level Maulidur Rasul Tokoh Wira Negara Award. I only made arrests," he said.

items.title: Singapore checkpoint bust: Malaysian man held, 700 cartons seized
items.summary: SINGAPORE: A 30-year-old Malaysian man was arrested after Singapore authorities found more than 700 cartons and 100 packets of duty-unpaid cigarettes hidden in his car at the Woodlands Checkpoint. Singapore's Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) said in a social media post that its officers directed the Malaysian-registered vehicle for enhanced checks on Aug 10. The contraband items were found hidden in modified compartments throughout the vehicle.

items.title: Pakistan and Iran made 'significant progress' in talks on conflict, minister says
items.summary: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan and Iran made "significant progress" in talks that focused on the US-Israeli war on Iran and a path to peace, Pakistan's interior minister said on Tuesday, at the end of a visit to Teheran. Talks between the two sides focused on measures to prevent further escalation, reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and an expedited termination of the conflict, a statement from the Pakistani military said about the meeting between the country's army chief, Asim Munir, and the Iranian leadership. Munir spoke with US President Donald Trump ahead of his Teheran visit, Reuters reported on Monday.

items.title: Prime Minister confirms Felda forensic audit proposal will be tabled at Cabinet meeting soon
items.summary: SERDANG, Aug 25 — A proposal for a forensic audit to be conducted into the management of the Federal Land Consolidation and Rehabilitation Authority (Felda) will be discussed by the Cabinet, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar was responding to a question about Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi’s suggestion that a forensic audit be conducted to determine whether there had been abuse of power, breach of trust or governance violations in Felda’s management. Previously, Anwar said he would await the full report by the special task force investigating Felda’s management issues before making any official announcement.

items.title: PM: Maulidur Rasul a time to practise Prophet Muhammad's teachings
items.summary: SERDANG: Maulidur Rasul should not be viewed merely as a celebration but as a chance for Muslims to appreciate and apply the teachings of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) in their daily lives. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the true significance of commemorating the Prophet's birth lay in how his teachings and values were reflected in the conduct of Muslims and their contribution to society. He said this required Muslims to demonstrate good values, respect, justice and excellence in their daily lives rather than merely displaying their faith through outward activities.

items.title: Washington Post ordered to rehire fired columnist
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The Washington Post was ordered Monday to reinstate columnist Karen Attiah, who was fired over social media posts she wrote in the aftermath of right-wing influencer Charlie Kirk's assassination. Attiah wrote on social media afterward that she would not display sadness for Kirk's killing and shared the activist's past racist comments about Black women. An arbitrator ordered the Post on Monday to rehire Attiah and compensate her with back pay, writing in the decision that the Post "did not have good and sufficient cause" for her dismissal.

items.title: Immigration lodges police report after viral UTC Pudu post found inconsistent with CCTV records
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 25 — The Immigration Department of Malaysia (JIM) has lodged a police report over a viral post concerning an applicant’s experience at the UTC Pudu Sentral Immigration Branch Office. Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said a review found that several allegations in the post were inconsistent with closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage, related records and statements from officers on duty at the time of the incident. A police report has been lodged and JIM will provide its full cooperation to the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM),” he said.

items.title: Thailand car production rises 6.1pct on year in July
items.summary: BANGKOK: Car production in Thailand rose 6.12 per cent in July from a year earlier to 117,383 units, the Federation of Thai Industries (FTI) said on Tuesday. July domestic car sales rose 20.07 per cent versus a rise of 17.26 per cent in June, the federation said. Exports in July rose 2.39 per cent compared to a drop of 7.45 per cent in the previous month, according to the FTI.

items.title: 'We're going to keep going': Venezuelan quake rescuers soldier on
items.summary: TWO months after two huge earthquakes struck Venezuela and killed thousands, volunteer rescuer Domingo Pacheco still faces a mountain of work. "The oxygen was slowly taken away from me until I kind of lost consciousness," Pacheco told AFP. Pacheco asked.

items.title: Haze alert: Penang health exco advises face masks as API levels spike
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 25 — Residents of Penang are urged to limit outdoor activities as air quality deteriorated today, with three of the state's four monitoring stations breaching the unhealthy threshold. State youth, sports and health committee chairman Daniel Gooi advised the public to wear face masks when outdoors to mitigate the effects of the poor air quality. According to the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), readings as of 11am showed unhealthy levels across most of the state.

items.title: 'Militants tracked my jogging routine' - Ayob Khan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Being constantly on guard became second nature to former deputy inspector-general of police Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay, particularly during his years at the forefront of the country's fight against terrorism. Ayob revealed that Islamic State-linked militants had recruited Malaysians through social media to monitor security personnel, including tracking the movements and routines of senior police officers. Ayob also defended the need for specialised legal tools such as the Security Offences (Special Measures) Act 2012 (Sosma) as he said the law remained important in tackling serious security threats, particularly terrorism and organised crime.

items.title: Social media, popular culture threatening Muslim identity, says Sultan Nazrin
items.summary: IPOH: Social media, popular culture, entertainment and global lifestyles are increasingly shaping the minds of younger generations and posing serious challenges to Muslim character and the identity of the ummah. Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah said Muslims must strike a careful balance between embracing modernity and preserving their religious principles and identity. Also present were Raja Permaisuri Perak Tuanku Zara Salim, Raja Muda of Perak Raja Jaafar Raja Muda Musa, Raja Di-Hilir Perak Raja Iskandar Dzulkarnain Sultan Idris and Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad.

items.title: Tighter Iran curbs could raise risks for Malaysian firms
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia could face some financial and trade-related risks if ship-to-ship transfers involving sanctioned Iranian oil continue off its waters, economists said. UniKL Business School economic analyst Associate Professor Dr Aimi Zulhazmi Abdul Rashid said Malaysian shipping companies, ports, insurers and banks that facilitate these sales of Iranian oil could face secondary sanctions such as frozen US assets and cut off from its financial system. "Reports have flagged ship-to-ship transfers of Iranian oil in international waters off Malaysia as part of Iran's 'dark fleet' operations.

items.title: MACC probes RM80m Felda Palong 7 oil palm replanting scheme after settlers raise concerns
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) is examining information related to the implementation of the oil palm development and replanting programme at Felda Palong 7 in Wilayah Raja Alias, Bandar Sri Jempol, Negeri Sembilan, including concerns over the quality of the seedlings supplied and their compliance with the required specifications. In a statement, MACC said the information was received from Pertubuhan Badan Bertindak Generasi Palong (Perbagi) chairman Mohd Syahrizal Md Yusuf, who raised concerns over the quality of the oil palm seedlings and the implementation of the programme. The commission said the matters raised included the supply, delivery, storage and age of the oil palm seedlings, as well as whether they complied with the required specifications.

items.title: Sultan Nazrin: True love for Prophet Muhammad means living by his teachings
items.summary: Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah said the true measure of love for the Prophet was reflected not in words or ceremonies, but in how far his teachings, character and practices influenced daily conduct. Also present were Raja Permaisuri Perak Tuanku Zara Salim, Raja Muda Perak Raja Jaafar Raja Muda Musa, Raja Di-Hilir Perak Raja Iskandar Dzulkarnain Sultan Idris and Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad. Sultan Nazrin said a strong Muslim character must originate from within.

items.title: Cybersecurity must go hand in hand with cyber resilience
items.summary: Yet incidents continue to occur, not necessarily because security measures are inadequate but because we often confuse cybersecurity with cyber resilience. An organisation can hold multiple certifications and implement extensive security controls yet still suffer serious disruption when a critical system or dependency goes offline. Cyber resilience means designing systems and institutions to continue functioning despite any disruption.

items.title: Six months of war: 20 dead in 68 incidents near Hormuz, IMO says
items.summary: In total, 68 incidents have been confirmed by the International Maritime Organisation (IMO) in the Gulf and neighbouring bodies of water, the equivalent of one every 2.6 days. Across all incidents, at least 20 seafarers or port workers were reported killed, 35 wounded and one missing, the UN maritime agency said. Iran-flagged vessels were reported as being involved in four incidents.

items.title: MetMalaysia warns of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds across four states and Sarawak
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Four states in Peninsular Malaysia and Sarawak are expected to experience thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds until 1 pm today, according to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia). In Selangor, the areas forecast to be hit are Kuala Selangor, Sabak Bernam, Hulu Selangor and Gombak, while in Sarawak, the areas involved are Bintulu and several areas in Miri, namely Subis, Miri, Beluru and Marudi. Meanwhile, in a separate statement, MetMalaysia also issued a Tropical Storm Advisory (NARRA) after a tropical storm was detected in northwestern China today, but stressed that the phenomenon would not have a significant impact on Malaysia.

items.title: Penang Hindu Endowments Board urged to clarify temple demolition notice
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Former Penang Hindu Endowments Board (PHEB) commissioner and Urimai secretary-general Satees Muniandy has urged the board to clarify why the Seberang Prai City Council issued a demolition notice to a Hindu temple in Batu Kawan. "However, the said temple is on PHEB's land and the city council has no business issuing the notice," he said today. PHEB manages Hindu religious endowments, including temple land and property, in the state.

items.title: Pengerang peat fire still burning across area the size of 51 football fields
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI: Firefighters continue to battle a peat fire the size of 51 football fields along the Sebana Cove-Punggai Bypass road in Pengerang, with round-the-clock operations ongoing. Johor Fire and Rescue Department operations commander Baharuddin Idris said firemen had been working continuously to put out the flames since yesterday. However, firefighters faced several challenges, including difficult terrain, strong winds, limited water supply and hot, dry weather, which further complicated containment efforts.

items.title: [UPDATED] Amirudin to lead PH-BN cooperation talks for Melaka polls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Pakatan Harapan election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari has been entrusted with handling a potential tie-up with Barisan Nasional in the upcoming Melaka election. PH chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said this was decided following a meeting with Amirudin on Sunday. "Room for cooperation...

items.title: [UPDATED] Anwar: Felda forensic audit proposal to be brought to cabinet [WATCH]
items.summary: SERDANG: The proposal for a forensic audit into alleged wrongdoing involving the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) will be brought to the cabinet for discussion. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said this when met by reporters after the national-level Maulidur Rasul celebration today. Anwar had previously said Felda was burdened with nearly RM10 billion in debts and losses following years of management failures and excessive political interference.

items.title: Immigration lodges police report over viral UTC Pudu passport cover incident
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department has lodged a police report over a viral social media post by a woman who claimed she was humiliated and accused of stealing a passport cover at the UTC Pudu Immigration office. Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the department had reviewed closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage, relevant records and statements from officers on duty following the allegations. He said the review found that several claims made in the viral post were inconsistent with the CCTV footage, records and accounts obtained from officers.

items.title: Land, building issues among main causes of strata title delays
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Issues involving land, buildings, applicants and documentation have been identified as the four main reasons strata homeowners may wait years, in some cases more than two decades, to obtain their strata titles. Federal Department of Lands and Mines (Strata and Stratum Titles Division) director Danial Lee Abdullah said some homeowners viewed the lack of a strata title as a non-issue as long as they could continue living in their properties. Danial Lee said land issues could arise when structures were built across multiple lots, requiring lot amalgamation before titles could be issued.

items.title: [UPDATED]: Syed Azman named Tokoh Perdana Maulidur Rasul, Ayob Khan also honoured
items.summary: SERDANG: Weststar Group founder and managing director Tan Sri Dr Syed Azman Syed Ibrahim has been named the recipient of the 2026 national-level Tokoh Perdana Maulidur Rasul award. Others honoured included Islamic scholar Maulana Abdul Hamid Chin (Tokoh Agamawan), International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM) Professor Dr Ruzita Mohd Amin (Tokoh Wanita Madani), and former Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB) director-general Datuk Dr Ahmad Parveez Ghulam Kadir (Tokoh Saintis). Angkatan Belia Islam Malaysia (Abim) president Ahmad Fahmi Mohd Samsudin was named Tokoh Belia Harapan, while Laman Yasim from Sarawak received the Tokoh Keluarga Mithali award.

items.title: One-third seats could boost Sabah, Sarawak's federal leverage
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: Allocating one-third of parliamentary seats to Sabah and Sarawak could give the two states significantly greater influence over the formation of the federal government, analysts said. Political analyst Awang Azman Pawi said if Sabah and Sarawak held 78 seats, or roughly one-third of the current 222-seat Dewan Rakyat, the two states would need the support of just 34 MPs from the peninsula to reach the 112 seats required for a simple majority. Conversely, a Peninsular coalition seeking to govern without the support of Sabah and Sarawak would need to win 112 of the remaining 144 seats, or nearly 78 per cent.

items.title: Civil Defence Force vows safety review after trained sergeant dies from cobra bite
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — The Malaysia Civil Defence Force (APM) takes the fatal snakebite incident involving one of its personnel seriously and remains open to reviewing and improving safety measures, risk management and the implementation of activities from time to time. APM also confirmed that the 39-year-old was a trained personnel, with extensive experience in handling venomous animals and had been actively serving since 2010. “APM stresses that the venomous animal handling activity was carried out in accordance with the stipulated standard operating procedures (SOPs) and safety procedures.

items.title: Sarawak and Klang Valley worst hit as 30 spots in Malaysia breach ‘Unhealthy’ API levels
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Malaysia’s prolonged haze crisis showed no signs of abating today, with 30 monitoring stations nationwide recording “unhealthy” Air Pollutant Index (API) levels, according to data from the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS). Sarawak remained the epicentre of the country's worst air pollution. The IPD Serian monitoring station recorded the highest reading nationwide at 180, inching toward the “very unhealthy” threshold of 201.

items.title: 350 EV charging points planned for major highways by 2028
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 350 electric vehicle (EV) charging points will be installed across the North-South Expressway and East Coast Expressway 2 networks by 2028. "Under Phase II of the plan, 118 EV charging points across strategic locations are already operational, including at rest and service areas along the highways. "We are targeting 20 to 30 EV charging points at strategic locations along traffic corridors, particularly those with high potential for congestion during peak times," she said.

items.title: Anwar reflects on Prophet’s leadership, promises change and justice for Malaysia in Maulidur Rasul message
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said that he will continue striving to bring about change and reform ( islah ) for the country, taking the strategy of Prophet Muhammad SAW in establishing a new administration in the Arab region over 14 centuries ago as a reference. This resolve is a prerequisite for ensuring the essentials (daruriyat) in Maqasid Shariah, as expressed by Muhammad Imarah,” he said. In the same post, Anwar also shared the history and hardships faced by Prophet Muhammad SAW in establishing a new administration in the Arab region over 14 centuries ago.

items.title: Cool Japan: Human fridge chills workers in extreme heat
items.summary: HIGASHIOSAKA, (Japan): Feeling dizzy and unwell after cycling to work in Japan's punishing summer heat, warehouse worker Isao Tabuchi headed for his company's newest acquisition: a refrigerator for humans. Once you use it, it's very, very cool," Tabuchi, 51, told AFP in the western industrial city of Higashiosaka. Tokyo-based industrial equipment distributor Trusco Nakayama said it has sold more than 300 units of the "Do Hiemon Box" since April, priced at 1.5 million yen ($9,400).

items.title: Anwar applauds Sukma 2026 champions, urges youth to chase glory and carry Malaysia’s name worldwide
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari and the state government for their commitment and hard work in successfully hosting the 2026 Malaysia Games (Sukma). He also congratulated the athletes, coaches, officials and secretariat involved, saying Sukma was not merely about winning medals but also a platform for discovering talent and producing champions. Even sweeter, hosts Selangor emerged as the overall champions of Sukma 2026,” he said in a Facebook post last night.

items.title: India lifts four-year-long ban on wheat exports
items.summary: NEW DELHI: India has lifted a four-year-long ban on exports of wheat and wheat products in a bid to boost farmers' incomes, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) announced in an official notification, reported Xinhua. The export policy of wheat was revised from prohibited to free with immediate effect, the DGFT's notification said. Commenting on the decision to lift the ban, the country's Food and Public Distribution Secretary Sanjeev Chopra reportedly said that since domestic wheat prices were currently depressed, allowing exports of wheat and wheat products would increase domestic prices, thus boosting farmers' incomes and encouraging good sowing in the forthcoming season.

items.title: IKEA picks Kuching for first-ever small store format in Malaysia, eyes December opening
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — IKEA Malaysia has confirmed that its first store in East Malaysia will open its doors in Kuching this December, marking a significant expansion into Sarawak after years of serving the state solely through e-commerce and delivery. IKEA Malaysia revealed that the new outlet will be the retailer's first small-format store, building on IKEA's existing e-commerce and fulfilment presence in the state. IKEA Kuching will become the company's fifth physical store in Malaysia, joining IKEA Damansara, IKEA Cheras, IKEA Tebrau and IKEA Batu Kawan.

items.title: MCA will not cooperate with DAP in polls, says sec-gen
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: MCA will not cooperate with DAP in upcoming elections, including the next Melaka polls, says secretary-general Datuk Chong Sin Woon. Chong said MCA's stance was in line with a resolution passed at its annual general assembly last year. Previously, BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said that any decision on political alliances must account for local sentiment.

items.title: MetMalaysia warns of sustained hot spell, 17 areas nationwide placed under caution status
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) today issued a Level 1 (caution category) hot weather status for 17 areas across Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak. In a statement, MetMalaysia said 11 of the affected areas are in Peninsular Malaysia, involving Larut and Matang, Kuala Kangsar, Kampar and Batang Padang in Perak; Kuala Krai in Kelantan; Kuantan, Raub, Temerloh and Pekan in Pahang; as well as Hulu Selangor and Gombak in Selangor. MetMalaysia said the Level 1 hot weather alert is issued when the maximum daily temperature in an area reaches between 35 and 37 degrees Celsius for at least three consecutive days.

items.title: Hot weather alert issued for 17 areas including Perak and Sabah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) today issued a Level 1 hot weather alert for 17 areas across Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak. MetMalaysia said the Level 1 hot weather alert is issued when the maximum daily temperature in an area reaches between 35 and 37 degrees Celsius for at least three consecutive days. The public can refer to MetMalaysia's official website for the latest daily hot weather updates nationwide.

items.title: Sabah smugglers jump into sea, abandon RM601,400 cigarette smuggling haul
items.summary: TAWAU: A group of smugglers dived into the sea to escape a police raid early yesterday, abandoning two boats loaded with cigarettes worth RM461,400. Marine Police Commander Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Amri Rahman said the raid followed intelligence and monitoring after it detected suspicious movements in the area. "In the raid, the team found 250,000 sticks of Premium International brand white cigarettes worth RM375,000 and 48,000 sticks of Menara Dunia branded cigarettes worth RM86,400," he said.

items.title: Police say Pasir Mas crash kills elderly woman and granddaughter, third victim hospitalised with injuries
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 25 — An elderly woman and her granddaughter were killed after the Perodua Axia they were travelling in veered off the road and crashed into a tree along Jalan Pasir Mas-Rantau Panjang near Culvert 5 in Pasir Mas yesterday. In the 11.20 am incident, the 73-year-old woman, who was seated in the rear, died at the scene, while her 23-year-old granddaughter, who was seated in the front, died while receiving treatment at Pasir Mas Hospital. Pasir Mas district police chief ACP Mazlan Hassan said the car was driven by another granddaughter of the victim, an 18-year-old girl, who suffered a fractured wrist and internal injuries and is receiving further treatment at the same hospital.

items.title: Will Tian Chua contest Batu again? Returning PKR veteran eyes political revival
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Former PKR vice-president Tian Chua has set his sights on a return to Parliament and is open to contesting his former stronghold of Batu, citing enduring grassroots support from the constituency. Tian Chua represented Batu for two consecutive terms after winning the seat in 2008. Despite the political fallout, Tian Chua claimed that his ties to the grassroots remain intact.

items.title: Police confirm Kajang road closures as Merdeka Eve celebration rehearsals roll out
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Five main roads around Kajang will be closed in stages from this Wednesday before being fully closed on Aug 30 in conjunction with the 2026 Selangor State Merdeka Eve Celebration at Kajang Stadium. Kajang District Police Chief ACP Naazron Abdul Yusof said the road closures were aimed at ensuring smooth traffic flow and public safety throughout the programme scheduled for Aug 30. He said Jalan Mahkamah would be fully closed from Aug 26 to 30, while four other roads — Jalan Cempaka Putih, Jalan Cempaka Kuning, Jalan Stadium and Jalan Cheras — would be closed in stages.

items.title: Ten arrested in Sandakan after woman found bound, murdered in home
items.summary: SANDAKAN, Aug 25 — Police have arrested 10 suspects, including two primary individuals, following the brutal murder of a 62-year-old woman whose decomposing body was discovered bound inside a toilet in Tanah Merah, Jalan Leila, last Tuesday. Sandakan District Police Chief ACP George Abd Rakman confirmed the discovery. “The discovery was made after police received information from the public at around 8.10pm regarding a foul smell coming from the house.

items.title: Selangor marks Sukma victory with Sept 1 holiday, honouring athletes and 10,000 volunteers
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 25 — The Selangor government has declared Sept 1 as a special holiday to commemorate the state contingent’s success in winning the overall title at the 2026 Malaysia Games (Sukma), held in Selangor. Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari announced the decision at the Games’ closing ceremony at Aneka Walk, SA Sentral, here yesterday, adding that it was a token of appreciation from the state government to the entire Selangor contingent for bringing honour to the state. Amirudin also expressed his appreciation to all parties who supported the Selangor contingent throughout the Games.

items.title: Worth the bargain? Malaysian consumers win big on Pinduoduo as local sellers cry foul
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 —Inside the sprawling digital storefront of Chinese e-commerce titan Pinduoduo, Shaun Kong routinely finds exactly what he didn't know he was looking for. He uses it to purchase routine lifestyle items—clothing, accessories, and unbranded goods. Is this Chinese dumping?

items.title: High Court dismisses Negeri Sembilan state government’s bid to evict Undangs from official halls, residences
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 24 —The High Court here today dismissed two applications by the Negeri Sembilan government seeking an immediate eviction involving the official halls and residences of the Undang of Rembau and Undang of Sungei Ujong. Judge Roz Mawar Rozain ruled through an online proceeding that the state government lacked legal standing (locus standi) to initiate the proceedings under Order 89 of the Rules of Court. The court ruled that the disputed premises are classified as reserved land under the National Land Code (NLC), rather than ordinary state land.

items.title: Man jailed three months, fined RM400 for impersonating MACC officer
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 —An unemployed man was sentenced to three months' jail and fined RM400 in the Selayang Magistrate's Court here today after pleading guilty to impersonating a Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) officer. Mohd Izham Mohd Zainuddin, 34, received the sentence from Magistrate Chai Guan Hock and was ordered to start his jail term from the date of arrest on July 30, 2026. The court also ordered the accused to be sentenced for a month if he failed to pay his fine.

items.title: PM Anwar inaugurates Malaysia’s latest film landmark
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today officially opened the National Film Development Corporation Malaysia (Finas) Tower in Damansara, marking a new phase in strengthening Malaysia’s film and audiovisual industry under the Orange Economy framework. Prime minister Anwar Ibrahim said the new Finas Tower marks a new chapter in strengthening Malaysia’s film and audiovisual industry as part of the Orange Economy. Communications and Multimedia Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Menara Finas, developed on a 5.14-acre site, began construction on January 20, 2021, and has now become the country’s new film industry hub.

items.title: Shoplot housing Village Park restaurant in Uptown Damansara set for RM5.3m auction
items.summary: A court document sighted by Malay Mail shows that the three-and-a-half-storey intermediate shopoffice at No. The document also states Standard Chartered Bank Malaysia Berhad's mortgage issuance date for the property is November 20, 2012. As for the auction, it was ordered by the High Court in Kuala Lumpur, with the document citing court orders dated January 8 and July 23 this year.

items.title: High Court dismisses bid to forfeit RM21m, gold bar seized from Aman Palestin
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 24 — The High Court here today dismissed the prosecution’s application to forfeit funds amounting to RM21 million, including foreign currency totaling US$139,650.68, which had been frozen under the name of the company Aman Palestin Berhad (Aman Palestin). The forfeiture application also involved a one-kilogram gold bar that was previously seized. Judge Datuk Seri Latifah Mohd Tahar, who is now a Court of Appeal Judge, made the decision after examining and listening to the written and oral submissions from both the prosecution and the respondent, Aman Palestin.

items.title: Penang enforces Private Accommodation By‑Laws, vows crackdown on unlicensed short‑term rentals
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 24 — The enforcement of the Private Accommodation By-Laws 2026 marks a crucial step in ensuring that short-term accommodation operators run their businesses legally and in compliance with regulations. President of the Malaysian Budget and Business Hotel Association (MyBHA), Dr Sri Ganesh Michiel, said the move is also vital to protect the safety of residents and tourists, while ensuring fairness and legal compliance. Penang became the first state in the country to enforce the Private Accommodation By-Laws effective Aug 1, to strengthen the regulation and enforcement of private accommodation operations.

items.title: Twins Serene and Irene Lock clinch top honours at Malaysia’s BEM Engineering Awards
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — Identical twins Dr Serene Lock Sow Mun and Irene Lock Sow Mei, 36, who have shared a classroom since primary school, achieved national recognition after being named among Malaysia’s top engineers at the Board of Engineers Malaysia (BEM) Engineering Awards ceremony last night. Sow Mun, an associate professor at Universiti Teknologi Petronas (UTP) became the first woman to win the National Young Engineer Award, while her sister Sow Mei, a senior process engineer at Petronas, received the Special Mention International Engineering Award (SMIEA) 2026. This recognition motivates me to contribute even more to the engineering field,” Sow Mei told Bernama.

items.title: MetMalaysia warns of evening storms across peninsula, Sabah, Sarawak
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning for parts of eight states and territories, warning residents to brace for heavy downpours, strong winds, and lightning strikes until 6:00pm today. According to the advisory issued at 3:55pm, severe convective weather is expected across several districts in Peninsular Malaysia, Sarawak, and Sabah. In Peninsular Malaysia, the warning covers Kulim, Baling, and Sik in Kedah, alongside Jeli and Gua Musang in Kelantan.

items.title: Malaysia Airlines retimes KLIA flights as airspace closes for National Day flypast rehearsals
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — Malaysia Airlines Bhd will retime selected flights arriving at and departing from KL International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1 following temporary airspace closures in conjunction with the 69th National Day celebrations. The national airline said the temporary closures within the Kuala Lumpur Terminal Control Area are to facilitate rehearsals and the National Day Flypast 2026, resulting in scheduled aircraft take-offs and landings at KLIA being temporarily suspended during selected periods. Malaysia Airlines also reminded passengers that check-in counters close 60 minutes before scheduled departure for both domestic and international flights, while boarding gates close 30 minutes before departure.

items.title: Ex-Sabah women and children’s hospital director sues successor, top official over removal
items.summary: Dr Yogendra Panchalingam filed the suit at the High Court of Sabah and Sarawak in Kota Kinabalu on August 21. He named Sabah Health Department deputy director Datuk Dr Abd Kahar Abd Asis and his former deputy turned successor, Dr Christine Lu Shin Yeen, as defendants. Appointed as hospital director in March 2025, Dr Yogendra denied all allegations of sexual harassment levelled against him, including complaints lodged by Dr Lu and the hospital’s corporate communications unit head, Elleyvianna Murang.

items.title: Zara Qairina inquest hears olive‑green ‘Love And Peace’ journal altered, 64 sheets missing
items.summary: The 77th witness, forensic science lecturer and researcher from Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM) Dr Wan Nur Syuhaila Mat Desa, said the journals comprised a green journal marked W1, a pastel purple “Simple Style Book” journal (W2), a dark brown journal (W3) and an olive-green “Love And Peace” journal (WK9). Meanwhile, W2 contained only 53 sheets compared with 96 sheets in a new reference journal, meaning 43 sheets were missing, while W3 contained 77 sheets against 98 sheets in the reference journal, leaving 21 sheets missing. She said WK9 was received in worn and torn condition and contained only 54 sheets compared with 118 sheets in a new reference journal of the same type, meaning 64 sheets were missing.

items.title: Police tighten Malaysia–Thailand border security after Yala, Pattani, Narathiwat blasts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — Police have stepped up security preparedness at the Malaysia-Thailand border following a series of explosions and attacks in Yala, Pattani and Narathiwat, southern Thailand, with the areas remaining under control. He said PDRM was also strengthening its prevention, early detection and rapid response approaches, as well as increasing intelligence and information sharing with Thai security agencies. Mohd Yusri said so far there were no reports of Malaysians being affected in the incident.
